transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
A second and final day of U.S.-led peace talks between Russia and Ukraine has wrapped up
in Abu Dhabi.
The meeting marks the first direct negotiations between the two sides since last February.
It comes amid a new push for a broader peace deal by the White House.
And Piers Charles Mains has more from Moscow.
These talks delivered just one concrete result.
Russian Ukraine agreed to another large-scale prisoner exchange.
Yet Jared Kushner, the White House envoy and President Trump's son-in-law, said quite good
progress had been made on the issue of security guarantees for Ukraine, a topic U.S. officials
have suggested could involve a rethinking of Europe's entire security architecture with
Russia and lead to future concessions that stop the actual fighting.
Kushner said he and fellow envoy Steve Whitcoff will fly to Moscow Thursday to brief Russian
President Vladimir Putin before heading to Ireland for a similar meeting with Ukrainian
President Vladimir Zelensky.
Charles Mains, NPR News, Moscow.
Stocks opened mixed this morning as the U.S. Treasury Secretary calls for a more balanced
relationship between the world's two biggest economies.
And Piers Scott Horsley reports the Dow Jones industrial average slipped about 30 points
in early trading.
Treasury Secretary Scott Besant says the U.S. needs to produce more and China needs to consume
more.
Besant spoke at a New York gala last night ahead of President Trump's visit to Shenzhen
next week, where he'll meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping.
China's consumption is likely to get a boost from Singles Day, which starts today.
The online shopping promotion is a kind of cross between Prime Day, Black Friday and
Valentine's Day.
Crude oil prices perked up a bit, but retail gasoline prices continue to fall.
AAA says the average price of regular gas dipped to $3.94 a gallon.
The U.S. bond market is closed in honor of Veterans Day.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
The Kennedy family has joined the legal fight against President Trump's proposed triumphal
arch in Washington, D.C.
They say it would cast a shadow over their ancestors' gravesites.
And Piers Rachel Treisman has more.
Nine members of the Kennedy family filed a motion in federal court late Tuesday to oppose
the 250-foot arch.
People are the children of Senator Robert F. Kennedy, though Health and Human Services
Secretary RFK Jr. is not included.
The Kennedys say the arch would obstruct views and cast shadows over their relatives' graves
at Arlington National Cemetery, including the John F. Kennedy eternal flame.
That's one of many arguments in the fight against the arch, which now includes Vietnam
War veterans, as well as the governments of D.C., Virginia and Arlington County.
A federal judge has blocked any construction through at least next Thursday.
Rachel Treisman, NPR News.
On Wall Street, the Dow has still done more than 30 points.
You're listening to NPR News.
Stock shares of computer chip maker Nvidia have fallen this week.
That's because it's been since Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang admitted having an affair.
Officials at Nvidia say that they are investigating whether he was the "target of a foreign intelligence
effort."
Now, both he and the company face a lawsuit from shareholders.
The lawsuit alleges that investors have been deceived about the effect of the news.
Pope Leo leaves Argentina today for the final leg of his 12-day tour of Latin America.
In his last days in the South American country, he spoke to prisoners and survivors of Argentina's
dirty war, and to young people he warned of the ills of vanity, and Piers Carey-Kahn has
more.
"Crowds have been massive for the Pope's packed schedule in Argentina.
He told a huge gathering of young Argentines and Buenos Aires to reject 'idols of our time.'
He warned against a long list of dangers, including money, drugs, porn, and an obsession
with popularity, appearance, and pleasure.
Leo urged youth to "not bow down before anything that cannot give you life."
Anticipation for Leo's Peru visit is huge.
The pontiff lived here for two decades and became a naturalized Peruvian citizen.
The Vatican is calling his Peru Stapa homecoming.
Peruvian officials launched a Pope weather watch as much of the country is under a state
of emergency with heavy rains forecast due to El Nino.
Terry Kahn, NPR News, Chicleo, Peru.

Kushner and Witkoff to brief Putin in Moscow, then meet Zelensky in Ireland

Singles Day shopping festival begins in China ahead of Trump's Shenzhen visit
AAA reports national average regular gasoline price falls to $3.94 a gallon
Kennedy family files federal court motion opposing Trump's 250-foot triumphal arch in Washington
Federal judge blocks construction of Trump's arch through at least next Thursday
Nvidia shares fall after CEO Jensen Huang admits affair; company probes foreign intelligence angle
Shareholders sue Nvidia alleging investors were deceived about effects of CEO's affair
Pope Leo warns Argentine youth against idols of money, drugs, pornography, and vanity
